newsitem.title: Italy: ALPINE SKIING-GOETSCHL SAVES DAY FOR AUSTRIAN WOMEN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GOETSCHL SAVES DAY FOR AUSTRIAN WOMEN.

text.p: Austrian Renate Goetschl finally gave her country something to celebrate at the Alpine skiing world championships on Saturday.

With nothing more to show for their efforts than three bronze medals and the championships drawing to a close, the Austrian team earned gold in the last women's event of the championships as Goetschl won the combined.
The largest and richest team on the Alpine circuit, with the Austrian government and sponsors backing them to the tune of some $4 million, had come under attack at home for a lack of results.
Particularly under fire were the women who had not won a title since Karin Buder's slalom gold in 1993.
"Austria has always been considered number one in the world when it comes to skiers," said Goetschl. "The world was looking at us.
"The press has been writing negative articles and everyone expected more from us."
Not many people however, expected much from the immensly talented but erratic Goetschl, who had not completed a slalom in a year before Thursday.
Instead the Austrians had pinned their medal hopes on veteran Anita Wachter, whose record includes four combined medals, including an Olympic gold and silver.

But after the slalom, which should have been the second half of the combined but became the first when the downhill had to be twice postponed because of bad weather, Goetschl was in seventh, one spot ahead of her team mate.

"The biggest advantage for me was having the slalom before the downhill," said Goetschl. "It was particularly good for me because I have only finished one slalom in two years and finishing the race gave me confidence."
Ironically, Goetschl burst onto the Austrian ski scene in 1993 with a victory in only her second World Cup race -- a slalom in Lillehammer.
Despite her early success in the technical events, Goetschl soon began to frustrate her coaches who said she was unable or unwilling to do what they told her.

This season she switched from the technical to the speed events and found immediate success winning a downhill in Vail and finishing second in Laax. In six giant slaloms this season her best result is an 18th while she has yet complete a slalom.

"I've really worked hard on my giant slalom this season but I'm focusing more on the downhill and super-G," said the 21-year-old skier. "Maybe in a few years I will be able to do them all equally well."
